sources.entry: paaster - End-to-end encrypted pastebin built with the objective of simplicity. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Paaster is an end-to-end encrypted pastebin focused on simplicity and privacy, with paste history and a CLI tool.
summary.what_it_does: Paaster lets users paste code or text that is encrypted locally in the browser with a secret the server never receives, so only people with the share link can view it. Pastes are stored with client and server secrets in IndexedDB, which enables a paste history and later modification or deletion. Users can set pastes to delete after viewing or after a set time, share them via QR code, and drag and drop files. A "Send to device" feature transfers a paste to another device using a short-lived 5-minute code and crypto_box_seal encryption. The README also lists keyboard shortcuts, themes, i18n support, and a CLI tool. Encryption uses libsodium functions via libsodium-wrappers-sumo.
use_cases: send a paste from phone to desktop
one-time paste that deletes after viewing
share files via a link with QR code
notable: End-to-end encryption where the secret key stays in the URI fragment and never reaches the server
Send to device transfer between your own devices using a 5-minute code and captcha
Paste history kept in browser IndexedDB
Dependencies are not dynamically loaded from third parties; uses package-lock.json and Socket.dev against supply chain attacks
caveats: The README states that you cannot trust an instance hosted by someone else, since its operator could expose your secret key; it recommends self-hosting or a trusted instance.
Client secrets in IndexedDB make it vulnerable to malicious JavaScript present at build time, per the README.
The README does not describe deployment steps; it refers to an external documentation site.
keywords: send files to my other device
